text: Watch for difficult delivery: the last piglet born more than 40 minutes ago, or the sow showing fatigue and rapid breathing. Common causes and responses: uterine inertia (weak contractions) — inject 1 cc oxytocin and wait 10 minutes for contractions to resume and the next piglet to be expelled; improper piglet presentation or an oversized piglet — a manual check by smooth palpation to assess piglet and leg position, followed by 3 days of antibiotic (e.g. TMP + Sulfa) for the sow. Managing improper presentation: for a stuck shoulder, extend the legs carefully without damaging the uterus; for a breech presentation, hook an index finger under the hock of a hind leg and extend it; for an oversized piglet, grasp the head with fingers and use a snare around the neck to assist. With a large litter (more than 10 piglets), the sow tires and contractions weaken, so later piglets can be weakened from staying too long in the birth canal — checking and assisting the final phase of delivery can save one or two piglets. The placenta is usually delivered 2–4 hours after the last piglet; injecting 2 cc oxytocin into the muscle once delivery is complete helps ensure no piglet is retained and the placenta is fully expelled.
